# Turboslide focus round, verification (pass 2)

The verifier's second report, on the merged tree after the fix round: `main` at `2b12e31` plus the seven lanes' merge 1 work and the fixers' edits of 2026-09-16, with one commit landing on the shared checkout during the pass (`b50e38f`, 18:32Z, `docs/gslides-parity/focus/AMENDMENTS.md` alone: the click model amendment A1; no code changed, so every run below measured the same code and `git diff` against `2b12e31` and `b50e38f` agree on every file but that one) (`git diff --stat 2b12e31`: 139 tracked files, 19,528 insertions, 39,912 deletions, plus the untracked focus files under `apps/studio/e2e/core/`, `scripts/probes/`, `docs/gslides-parity/focus/` and the new tests). Written 2026-09-16 (UTC times below). The binding specification is `docs/FOCUS.md` (sections 5 and 6), the audits under `docs/gslides-parity/focus/audit-*.md` are the reference for how a row is driven, and the orchestrator's three rulings on section 9 stand. Every command below was run by the verifier on this tree; nothing was taken on trust from a lane's note, and the fix round's notes (`build/b1.md` to `b7.md`, their "Fix round" sections) were read as claims to check. The verifier ran no git write command, no `pnpm install`, `pnpm add` or `pnpm exec` outside `scripts/check.mjs`, no build outside `scripts/check.mjs`, and no Docker (check step 25 was left out by the round's rule; a daemon answers on the machine). The fresh enforce preview of this pass is `https://turboslide-gikztnsgb-kl01s-projects.vercel.app`, deployed by the verifier at 17:41Z with `vercel deploy --yes --archive=tgz` from the repository root and the round four per deployment variables (`TURBOSLIDE_AUTHORIZE=enforce`, `TURBOSLIDE_REALTIME=blob`, `TURBOSLIDE_MAIL=off`, the public store host, the two secrets from `openssl rand -hex 32`, never printed), ready at 17:42Z; never `--prod`. ## 1. Verdict

The merged tree does not pass the gate of FOCUS.md 6.2 on the fresh enforce preview, and the tree's own chain is not green either; it is much closer than at pass 1.

- On the enforce preview `https://turboslide-gikztnsgb-kl01s-projects.vercel.app` (deployed by the verifier at 17:41Z from this tree), the core gate's rows read 329 passed, 60 failed and 1 not driven of 390 after the walk's stopped areas were driven again alone (section 3): 229 rows pass here and in pass 1's last preview run, 100 newly pass (the fix round's rows among them: `decks.trash.delete-forever-enter`, `export.pdf.notes-honest`, `export.print.download-pdf-follows-preview`, `text.format-menu.text-fitting`, `surface.parked-shortcut-unbound`, `surface.parked-blocks-render`, `decks.home.new-presentation`, the images rows, the arrange rows, 16 of 20 shapes rows), and 8 newly fail (`decks.access.paint`, `text.format-menu.align-left`, `share.stranger-cannot-edit`, `export.print.layout-with-notes`, `export.print.file-menu-after-close`, `help.documentation-link`, and the two finally rows the verifier's stop failed). `present` is the one feature with every row passing (18 of 18); `help` misses one row by a GitHub 429 to the runner; every other feature has a failed row and is parked at a ship made from this tree by rule 4; `surface.advanced.remembered` fails, which blocks the ship on its own.
- The core walk stalled for nine and a half minutes on the preview inside a window API `asset.add` that never answered (F-stall); the verifier stopped the probe, the gate went on to the specs, and the areas the stop left not driven were driven alone in two more walks (the images area's `asset.add` returned in about a second both times after). The gate itself is fixed (pass 1's F3): it printed its verdict and wrote its files on every run, `retries` zero.
- Fourteen text rows fail in the walk's state on the preview and pass by hand on a fresh box (F-text-state), while the autofit row fails on the product (F-autofit) and the Format > Text > Size row does nothing on a list block (F-list-size). The share rows fail on two product mechanisms read by hand: the dialog's second Copy link in a session is refused as stale ("the access record is at revision 0, not 1") and a minted Edit link answers 404 to its visitor for a while (F-share-copy, F-share-404). The reply to a comment is not listed (F-comments-reply). A restore from the Version history panel changes nothing (F-versions). Ruling (2)'s restricted default holds where the access record is read, and one hand run saw a View link's visitor receive the editor at `/edit/<id>` when the record read as absent (F-missing-record: `TURBOSLIDE_MISSING_RECORD` unset means a recordless deck is a legacy editor deck).
- The two views hold: with Advanced tools off, none of the 171 parked ids is drawn in any menu, submenu, the toolbar or the two right click menus at 1440 or at 390; with it on, 136 of them are drawn and the Extensions menu returns; the setting survives a reload and is off in a fresh browser (section 6). The title row's inbox plate, own chip and own roster row leave with the switch (b1's fix round).
- The tree's gates: `tsc -b` exit 0; check step 5 red on two `apps/cli` tests that time out under the machine's load and pass alone (pass 1's F1 and F2 are closed); check step 3 red by design on the uncommitted tree; check step 19 red on 88 unformatted files, 15 of them this round's; `tokens.css` byte identical to `2b12e31`; the default view words test passes; `what-works.mjs --check` passes; the hosted smoke 40 of 40 and the new write probe every step on the preview. On the verifier's 4368 dev server (tmp store, memory channel, shadow mode) the same drivers read 338 passed, 51 failed, 1 not driven of 390 (2204 s, retries zero); 309 rows pass on both origins. Locally the comments rows pass 7 of 7 and the surface rows 8 of 8; the two share refusal rows fail by shadow mode's floor alone; the sixteen title and caret rows of the text area fail on the dev server's state as in pass 1; the rows that fail on both origins (the Format menu's Size and Align rows in the walk's state, the autofit growth, the layout runs, the show's link and picture, the hex field, the Transparency drag, the Arrange > Order rows in the walk's state, the zoom step from Fit, the two tab paste, the shape exports, the restore, the two export driver rows) are section 5's.
- Shapes: under ruling (1) Insert > Shape leaves the default view for this ship and Line and Arrow leave with it (`shapes.export.pdf`, `shapes.export.pptx` and three driver read rows fail on the preview; 16 of 20 shapes rows and 4 of 5 lines rows pass; the parking edit, b3's R14, is not on the tree).

## 5. Findings

Severity as the orchestrator set it for this report: 3 a core row broken, 2 a core row flaky or a parked row visible by default (a red tree gate is filed at 2 as well), 1 cosmetic. The owner is the lane whose files carry the mechanism; the integrator where the merge or the ship step makes the edit. Every finding names the file and the evidence run; where a hand run on the preview settled a mechanism its scenario is named (`ver2/repro-scenarios.mjs`, records `ver2/repro-preview-p2-*.json`). Pass 1's findings are mapped at the end of this section.

Severity as the orchestrator set it: 3 a core row broken, 2 a core row flaky or a parked row visible by default (a red tree gate is filed at 2 as well), 1 cosmetic. The owner is the lane whose files carry the mechanism (B1 the surface, B2 text and slides, B3 objects, B4 the drivers, B6 access and sharing, B7 the server, or the integrator). Every finding names its evidence run; the run of record is the preview gate of C2.3 unless another is named. ## C2.9 For Kevin

1. The tree does not ship. On the fresh enforce preview 382 of 397 core rows pass after the rows a stall took were driven again alone, 14 fail and 1 is manual; a ship from these runs would park `decks`, `text`, `images`, `shapes`, `lines`, `present`, `share`, `comments` and `export` beside the two features already parked, and no `surface` row fails. The chain is red at steps 3 (by design), 19 (pre round files), 20, 21, 26, 31 and 32.
2. The saving stall came back. Ten minutes into the walk on the fresh preview the title row read "Saving..." and stayed there; the tab kept applying your edits (slides appeared) but the server never acknowledged them, and every setup after that timed out for eight minutes (C2-F24). The integrator's run of record saw the same on 2026-09-17T00:31Z; pass 1 did not; this pass did, on a deployment made from the fix round's tree. Nothing in the fix round touched the acknowledgement path, and the runtime log of the window is out of reach, so the mechanism is still unread. It is the first thing to fix before a ship: you would see "Saving..." forever and lose the edits on a reload.
3. The click model works as you asked, on the preview and locally: one click selects a box with its handles and chip and places no caret; a drag from anywhere inside moves it, and the whole selection when several are selected; a double click enters the text at the point; typing on a selected box replaces its text; Enter appends; Escape twice leaves it. ## C3.1 Verdict

The tree does not ship (FOCUS.md 6.2), and the gap has narrowed to one mechanism. On the preview of record the core gate's run of record reads 392 passed, 6 failed, 1 not driven (manual) of 399 in 40.9 min: the walk drove all 316 steps on one deck with no stall (`decks.save.acknowledged` passed, every A1 row passed, the one failed walk row is the parked `shapes.fill.colour`), and five spec rows failed, one of them a `surface` row. Driven again with the four failed spec files on the same deployment, the merged result under 6.2's last run rule reads 394 passed, 4 failed, 1 manual; 4 rows flipped between the two runs (C3-F4) and two failed in both (`decks.access.paint`, `present.skipped-left-out`). Every one of those six preview misses but the parked fill row is one mechanism, read on the wire from the five traces the gate kept: the tab's stream is refused `503 too_many_streams` by the instance's stream counters (4 per anonymous identity, 16 per IP), the room client posts nothing while its stream is down, and nothing reopens the stream for about a minute, so a window API write reads "Saving…" past its bound (C3-F1). The Blob store itself refused nothing in this pass: no 429 on any row, in any console, in the burst's three runs or in the deployment's runtime log followed from 03:15Z to the end, the new write probe passed all 27 steps on the preview, the A1 hand drive passed 18 of 18 on its first run, and the budget's constants, timers and unit tests read as the fix round says (C3.2a). The features a ship from these runs would park: `decks`, `present`, `share` and `shapes` beside the two already parked, and the flipped `surface` row fails the ship on its own. On the memory tier the verifier's 4389 read 395 passed, 3 failed (the three standing memory tier rows of C2-F21, whose fixes C3-R2 to C3-R4 are not on the tree), 1 manual, with every spec row passing, and the check’s 4321 read the same 395, 3 and 1 with the same three rows. The check chain is red at steps 3 (by design), 5 (under load; red twice, on child process and timing tests that pass alone), 19 (the pre round files and the evidence JSON), 20 (one check, the sidebar's native titles), 21 (13 editor spec tests), 26 (three two browser tests: the two parked rows and `realtime.spec.ts:374`, C3-F8), 31 (the perf budget: the standing bytes and DOM rows plus 22 timing rows under the load) and 32 (the three memory tier rows of C2-F21).

What this pass read as closed on the tree: the 429 and its sentences (C3-F2); the editor's crash into the router's page (C3-F3, pinned by the route's `errorComponent` and fourteen unit tests, driven by no e2e run of the boundary itself: the two probes of the integrator’s fixer and a variant of the verifier’s did not show the page on 4389, C3-F14); the late 500 and 404 answers of a single tab (C3-F5); the arrange paste row (C3-F6); `pnpm test` taking the lock (C3-F9); four of step 20's five checks (C2-F13 narrowed to the sidebar's `title`); the shape fill row on the memory tier (now C3-F7's flip). What stands: the stream cap stall (C3-F1, with C2-F6 and the flips of C3-F4 inside it), the parked fill row (C3-F7), the three memory tier rows (C2-F21), the two browser realtime suite (C3-F8, deterministic, B2’s text session base), the standing chain reds (C2-F12 widened, C2-F14, C2-F15, C2-F17, C2-F18), and three small ones (C3-F10, C3-F12, C3-F13).

### C3.2a The blob tier budget on the tree

The budget the fix round binds (one timed store call every 2 s per open deck per instance while a client stream is open, none otherwise; presence writes on a change alone at a 5 s floor with no retry loop; the SDK's retries off; a 429 or a 5xx backing the poll off to 60 s with the room telling its streams; nothing thrown by the store reaching the editor; every call under a deadline) was read in the code by the verifier, constant by constant and timer by timer, and the unit tests that pin it were run on the tree (the units row of C3.2). What the tree does:

| Rule                                                   | Where                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Read                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One timed call per 2 s per open deck per instance      | `packages/store/src/pulse.ts` (`HOSTED_POLL_MS` 2000, `POLL_CALLS_PER_MINUTE_MAX` 30, `PULSE_SAFETY_TICKS` 15), `packages/realtime/src/blob.ts` `startPulsePoll`                                                                                       | one `head` of `decks/<id>/.turboslide/pulse.json` per tick; on a moved etag the three reads (a forced sync of the store, the presence record, the comments index); on an unchanged etag `presence.confirm` and nothing else; every fifteenth tick the manifest head in place of the pulse (one call that tick too); the next tick is scheduled after the call returns (`setTimeout`, not an interval), so a slow call never stacks a second one |
| None when no stream is open                            | `blob.ts` `subscribe` (`SubscribeOptions.passive`), `apps/studio/src/server/room.ts` 527, `stopWatching`                                                                                                                                               | the room's own listener subscribes `{ passive: true }` and starts no poll; the first active listener (a client stream, `routes/api/decks.$deckId.stream.ts` 128) starts it, the last one's release stops it (`state.listeners <= 0`) and clears the pulse memory; on the blob tier the room installs no `store.watch` timer (`room.ts` 650) and no page calls `write.ts` `watchDeck`                                                            |
| Presence writes on a change alone, 5 s floor, no retry | `packages/store/src/presence-store.ts` (`PRESENCE_POLL_MS` 5000, `PRESENCE_PUSH_SPACING_MS` 5000, `PRESENCE_VOLATILE_FIELDS`)                                                                                                                          | `pushNow` is one `ifMatch` attempt and puts the pulse after the record; a lost race leaves the changes pending and schedules one push at the floor; `selection`, `follow` and `pointerOn` ride the next push and start none; `pollNow` reads and never writes; `roster()` reads the record on a presence post only when the pulse has not confirmed it inside `PRESENCE_POLL_MS`; the standalone `watch` timer has no caller on the blob tier   |
| The comments index on the pulse, no timer of its own   | `packages/store/src/comments-store.ts` `watchSidecarIndex` (`pollMs: null`), `room.ts` 188                                                                                                                                                             | the room wires the watch with `pollMs: null` and `{ poll, stop }`; the channel calls `poll()` when the pulse moved                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| The SDK's retries off                                  | `packages/store/src/blob-vercel.ts` `disableSdkRetries` (`VERCEL_BLOB_RETRIES=0` unless the deployment set it)                                                                                                                                         | set once at the client's construction; the caller's abort signal reaches every SDK call                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Backoff and the streams told                           | `pulse.ts` `isStoreBusy`, `storeRetryAfterMs`, `pollBackoffMs` (`POLL_BACKOFF_MAX_MS` 60 000); `blob.ts` `tick`; `protocol.ts` `store` event                                                                                                           | the tick doubled per failure to 60 s and never under the store's `retry-after`; `{ type: 'store', ok: false, retryAfterMs }` published once per outage and `{ ok: true }` on the first success; the room client reads it into `SyncStatus.storeDegraded` (`room-client.ts` 874); the title row's word for it (`TITLE_ROW.reconnecting`) is on the tree and not yet wired (b1 R46, b7 FR3-R4, FR3-R5)                                            |
| Nothing thrown by the store reaches the editor         | `room.ts` `storeBusyResult` (503 `store_busy`, `retry-after`), `admitOnBlob`; `routes/edit.$deckId.tsx` (`shouldReload: false`, `errorComponent: EditRefused`), `router.tsx` `defaultErrorComponent`, `editor/refusal.ts`, `controller.tsx` `onResync` | a refused write answers 503 with the product's sentence; a loader that throws draws the product's refusal page with Reload (the integrator's fixer); a store error in `onResync` becomes a snackbar sentence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Every call under a deadline                            | `packages/store/src/blob-store.ts` `boundedBlobClient` (`BLOB_READ_TIMEOUT_MS` 10 000, `BLOB_DOCUMENT_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS` 20 000, `BLOB_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS` 90 000)                                                                                        | the shared half (presence, comments, the pulse) runs over `boundedBlobClient(exportClient)` in `room.ts` 150                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

The unit tests that pin the budget, run by the verifier on the tree: `pulse.test.ts` "pins the budget: one timed call per tick is at most 30 a minute per open deck per instance" (the constants), `blob.test.ts` "makes one head of the pulse per tick while a stream is open, none for a passive listener, and none once the last stream closed" and "backs the poll off when the store refuses and tells the streams", `presence-store.test.ts` "pins the budget: reads on the tick, pushes on a change alone with a five second floor, a selection change starts none" and "reads on poll alone and never writes from it", `comments-store.test.ts` "runs no timer of its own with pollMs null", `hosted.test.ts` (the commit that met its deadline, the own claim, the mirror under a refusal, the listings joined), `blob-admission.test.ts` (the 503 answers), `room-client.test.ts` (the in flight echo, the replayed answer behind the position, the `store` event); the store package 15 files 190 passed, the realtime package 10 files 98 passed, the studio project 50 files 306 passed (C3.2). The cadence itself cannot be counted from outside a deployment (the store's calls leave the function and the runtime log carries the product's own lines alone), so the budget's evidence on the preview is the absence of the 429 sentence and of `blob: polling <deck> failed` in the runtime log followed through every run, the acknowledgement times of the gate and the burst, and the constants above.

## C3.5 Findings

Severity as the orchestrator set it: 3 a core row broken, 2 a core row flaky or a parked row visible by default (a red tree gate is filed at 2 as well), 1 cosmetic. The owner is the lane whose files carry the mechanism (B1 the surface, B2 text and slides, B3 objects, B4 the drivers, B6 access and sharing, B7 the server, or the integrator). Every finding names its evidence run; the run of record is the preview gate of C3.3 unless another is named. Pass 1's findings keep their numbers: one this pass closes is listed at the end with the run that closed it, one that stands is listed again with this pass's evidence, and a new one takes the next C3 number. The fix round's budget rule (a 429 sentence, a hang past 20 s or a cadence over the budget is a severity 3 finding for B7) is applied in C3-F1 and C3-F2.

The gate kept the five failed tests' traces (`ver6/gate-preview/run1/playwright/*/trace.zip`, read with `ver6/read-trace.mjs`), and every one shows the same sequence with no store call in it: (a) the tab's `GET /api/decks/<id>/stream?since=N&retire=…` is answered `503 {"error":"too_many_streams","cap":"identity"}` (`cap: "ip"` in the surface file) by the instance the reconnect landed on (`apps/studio/src/server/room.ts` `createStreamCounters`, `CAPS.streams` of `packages/realtime/src/admission.ts` 39: 4 open streams per anonymous identity, 16 per IP, 256 per instance, counted in the instance's memory and released when the route's `close()` runs); in `decks.access.paint` at 03:38:12Z after one 200 stream at 03:38:08Z, in `surface.parked-blocks-render` at 03:52:08Z after four streams of the same tab answered 200 within 10 s (0.5 s, 5.6 s, 8.8 s, 9.2 s), in `present.skipped-left-out` five refusals in a row (03:44:30Z to 03:44:35Z and 03:45:22Z), in `collab.edit-from-owner` one at 03:48:41Z. (b) The browser's `EventSource` reconnects on a 5xx with the server's `retry` (1 to 4 s, `sseRetry`), so the refusals come in bursts (the present trace: four attempts 1.3 to 1.9 s apart, every one refused, the cap not released between them); the transport (`apps/studio/src/editor/controller.tsx` `sseTransport`, `source.onerror`) reports "the stream closed" on each and the room client marks itself disconnected and schedules nothing of its own (`room-client.ts` 1132 `onError: () => { connected = false; emitStatus(); }`); the `retry-after: 5` the route sends with the 503 is read by nobody. (c) `flush()` returns while the stream is not connected (`room-client.ts` 915 `if (clientId === null |                                                                                                               | !connected) return;`), so the window API write stays pending with the title row on "Saving…" and no `POST /ops`leaves the tab: the traces hold no ops POST between the refusal and the next stream. (d) After the last refusal of a burst the traces hold no stream attempt for 47 to 61 s, then a`200`on the same`since`(03:39:13Z, 03:53:09Z), and the pending write posts and lands at once; what spaces that last refused attempt from the next by about a minute was not found in the product's code (the room client's`start()`runs once,`heartbeat()`posts presence alone,`BACKOFF_MAX_MS` is 8 s, the controller schedules no reopen), so the minute is recorded as measured, not explained. The runtime log of the deployment (`ver6/runtime-log.jsonl`, followed through every run) carries no 429, no `BlobTimeoutError`, no `blob: polling … failed`refusal and no line at the refusals' times; the store was not in the path. Why the caps fill: a core spec file runs its rows in one browser context (one identity, one IP; FOCUS.md 6.1), each editor page opens a stream (240 to 290 s lifetime), and a slot is released only when the instance that holds it runs the route's`close()` (the abort of the request, the lifetime timer, an access recheck); a page that navigates away leaves its slot held on that instance until the abort is seen, a reconnect can land on another instance, and four pages of one identity in a few minutes (or sixteen streams behind one IP) reach the cap on a fluid compute deployment. The rows the memory tier drives never meet it (one instance, one identity per context, the same specs 101 of 101 on 4389 and 4321). ## C3.9 For Kevin

1. The tree does not ship, and what stops it is now one thing. On the enforce preview built from this tree the gate's run of record reads 392 passed, 6 failed, 1 manual of 399; the walk went through all 316 steps on one deck with no stall this time, and after the four failed spec files were run again the merged result reads 394 passed, 4 failed, 1 manual, with 4 rows flipping between the two runs. Every preview miss but the parked shape fill row is the same mechanism (C3-F1): the tab's live stream is refused by the server's own cap on open streams (4 per anonymous person, 16 per network address, counted per instance and freed only when that instance notices the old stream closed), the editor sends no edit while its stream is down, and nothing reopens the stream for about a minute, so "Saving…" sits there past the 60 s bound. The traces of the five failed tests show it request by request; the Blob store is not in the picture any more.
2. The store budget you set holds on the tree. The server polls one small record per open deck every 2 s and only while someone has the deck open, presence writes land on a change with a 5 s floor and one attempt, the SDK's retries are off, every call has a deadline, and a refusal would back the poll off to a minute and tell the tabs. In this pass nothing refused: no "Too many requests" on any of the 399 rows in two full runs, in the burst's three runs, or in the deployment's runtime log followed the whole time; the hosted smoke read 40 of 40, the new write probe all 27 steps, the hand drive of the click model 18 of 18 at the first try. The one number to watch is the burst: run 1 made 71 writes with the slowest at 2.2 s, and runs 2 and 3 could not even open their deck because the burst's own companions had filled the stream cap for their address (the same C3-F1, a hang past 20 s, severity 3 for the server lane).
3. The click model works as you asked on every origin: one click selects with the handles and the chip and no caret, a drag from anywhere inside moves the box (and the whole selection), a double click enters the text at the point, typing on a selected box replaces its text, Enter appends, Escape twice leaves it. Every A1 row passed in both gates and in the hand drives (C3.7, screenshots under `ver6/a1/`), and this time the server never made them wait.
4. The tree does not ship (FOCUS.md 6.2), and the gap is narrower than pass 2 read it. Both walks drove all 316 steps on one deck with no stall, and a third walk under a 5 s window API bound drove them again with no call past 5 s (the "no Saving past 5 s" reading holds: 900 window API calls over three walks, every one answered inside its bound). Every row of the matrix passed in both runs on the memory tier as well: the local gate on 4395 (its second run, on a private tmp store; the first run's specs were voided by the machine's tmp cleaner, C3S-F5) and check step 32 on the check's own 4321 server read 398 passed, 0 failed, 1 manual, the first full green of step 32 this cycle (the three memory tier rows of C2-F21 and the parked fill row of C3-F7 pass: S3's four fixes are on the tree).

What stops the ship is the stream cap on the blob tier, read in three places this pass. The burst with three companions stalled in one of its three runs: four writes sat at or near the 60 s bound while the tab read `connected: true` and the server's revision moved past them, and the tab recovered only after 238 s, about the stream lifetime (C3S-F1, severity 3 for S1 by the round's rule: a write past 20 s); the runtime log for that window shows the address cap of one instance full (`address 16/16`, 14 to 16 identities) with the companions' streams, which the runtime never releases when a page goes. `decks.access.paint`'s failure is the same mechanism from a single tab: three quick navigations left slots the tab could never name (their opens were aborted before a hello), every later open was refused at the identity cap, the client reopened every 5 s exactly as the fix says, and with no hello the page had no client id to post with, so `deck.set` read Saving for 60 s (C3S-F2). The stream probe, five runs, read the root under both: on this deployment a closed raw stream's slot is not freed within `retry-after`, within 73 s or across four release cycles; it is freed by the lifetime timer or by the open landing on another instance (SEAM-F4 confirmed; the closer's reader gone check does not fire on the runtime). The second flaky row is the presence record's: a closed tab whose leave beacon is lost keeps its chip for 30 to 35 s and the row's bound is 30 s (C3S-F3). Beside these, one budget rule was broken on the wire once: a Blob 403 on a fresh deck's file left the ops and presence routes as 500 answers for eleven seconds on run 1's walk deck (C3S-F4; the rows passed, the room client re-posted). The store itself refused nothing: no 429, `BlobTimeoutError`, `store_busy` or `polling … failed` line in the runtime log followed from 10:24Z through the last run; the hosted smoke 40 of 40, the new write probe all steps, the A1 hand drive 18 of 18 on both origins.

### C3S.2a The blob tier budget on the tree

The budget the fix round binds (one timed store call every 2 s per open deck per instance while a client stream is open, none otherwise; presence writes on a change alone at a 5 s floor with no retry loop; the SDK's retries off; a 429 or a 5xx backing the poll off to 60 s with the room telling its streams; nothing thrown by the store reaching the editor; every call under a deadline) was read again on this tree. The round's prompt says the stream fix round adds no store call and changes no cadence; the verifier checked it by bytes: `git archive 540363f` (the checkpoint of the tree before this round) was unpacked into the scratchpad and every budget file compared with `cmp`. `packages/realtime/src/blob.ts`, `packages/store/src/pulse.ts`, `packages/store/src/presence-store.ts`, `packages/store/src/comments-store.ts`, `packages/store/src/blob-store.ts`, `packages/store/src/blob-vercel.ts`, `packages/store/src/hosted.ts`, `packages/realtime/src/admission.ts`, `packages/realtime/src/protocol.ts` and `packages/realtime/src/channel.ts` are byte identical to the checkpoint; so is `packages/chrome/src/tokens.css` (and to `2b12e31`). The constants read the values of pass 2's C3.2a: `HOSTED_POLL_MS` 2000, `POLL_CALLS_PER_MINUTE_MAX` 30, `PULSE_SAFETY_TICKS` 15, `POLL_BACKOFF_MAX_MS` 60 000 (`pulse.ts` 23 to 29); `PRESENCE_POLL_MS` 5000, `PRESENCE_PUSH_SPACING_MS` 5000 (`presence-store.ts` 58, 60); `BLOB_READ_TIMEOUT_MS` 10 000, `BLOB_DOCUMENT_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS` 20 000, `BLOB_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS` 90 000 (`blob-store.ts` 592 to 598); `SDK_RETRIES_VARIABLE` `VERCEL_BLOB_RETRIES` set to 0 by the client (`blob-vercel.ts` 109); the comments index on the pulse with `pollMs: null` (`room.ts` 189) and the room's own listener `{ passive: true }` (`room.ts` 528); `CAPS.streams` `{ anonymous: 4, signedIn: 8, agent: 4, ip: 16, instance: 256 }` untouched (`admission.ts` 39).

What this round added on the stream path, read in the code and pinned by the unit tests run in C3S.2: `STREAM_READER_GONE_MS` = 2 × `STREAM_HEARTBEAT_MS` + 5000 = 35 000 ms (`room.ts` 1995; the closer reads the controller's `desiredSize` at the writes the route already makes, the heartbeat every 15 s among them, so it adds no timer and no store call); `RETIRE_MAX` 8 on both sides (`room.ts` 1783, `room-client.ts` 156); the room client's `BACKOFF_MAX_MS` 8000 and `REOPEN_WAIT_MAX_MS` 60 000 (`room-client.ts` 152, 154); the route's `retry-after` of a refused open 5 s (`decks.$deckId.stream.ts` `STREAM_REFUSAL_RETRY_AFTER_S`). The room client's `flush()` now posts over `POST /ops` while its stream is down, which is a write the tab would have made anyway (one POST per burst, none new), and its reopen ladder waits the server's `retry-after` or `retry:` value and never bursts (the unit tests of `room-client.test.ts` and `realtime.spec.ts:543`).

### C3S.3a The stream cap probe

What the probe measures (`verification/cycle3-ship-stream-cap-probe.mjs`, the verifier's, with S1-R4's `describe` read from the seam step and this pass's release cycles): from one page of `/edit/gt-brand` (one anonymous identity with a stream of its own) six raw same origin stream fetches, held; every one closed client side and one open every 2, 5, 10, 20 and 30 s until admitted; then the release cycles: four times an open, held one second and closed, the next open waiting the last refusal's `retry-after` (5 s). The round's expectation: a closed stream's slot frees within `retry-after`, so the opens after the closes are admitted. The caps are per instance (`admission.ts` `CAPS.streams`, `createStreamCounters` per process) and the preview routes each open to whichever instance is warm, so a reading names the instance through `x-vercel-id` and the runtime log's refusal line (`identity n/4, address n/16, instance n/256 (k identities)`). The page's own `describe().state.sync` read `connected: true, streamDown: false, storeDegraded: false, offline: false` before and after every run (the page's stream is not what the probe cuts).

| Run                                 | Opens 1 to 6                                                                | After the close                                                    | Release cycles                                           | Runtime log                                                                                                                | Reading                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |

Read together with the seam step's section 5: on this deployment a closed raw stream's slot is never freed within `retry-after`; it is freed by the lifetime timer (240 to 290 s) or by the instance being left behind. The release the product has is the `retire` list (the ids a tab learned from its hellos, filtered to this deck and identity), which the two flaky preview rows of C3S.5 show is not enough: an open aborted by a navigation before its hello holds a slot the tab can never name (C3S-F2), and a fresh browser context's stream is a slot its identity never retires (the burst's companions, C3S-F1).

A cell reads the driver's own words on a miss. The counts by feature come first; "Passed everywhere" is the preview (both runs), 4395 and 4321. Three rows miss on some origin: two flaky on the preview alone (`decks.access.paint`, C3S-F2; `collab.presence-chips`, C3S-F3), both passed on both memory tier servers, and the manual paste row not driven everywhere. No row failed on the memory tier: the three rows of C2-F21 and the parked fill row of C3-F7 pass on 4395 and on 4321 (S3's fixes), and every A1 row passes on every origin.

## C3S.9 For Kevin

1. The tree does not ship yet, and the reason is now one mechanism with two faces. On the enforce preview built from this tree the gate ran twice and read 398 of 399 rows passed, then 396: two rows passed once and failed once (a flaky row fails the ship under your rule), and both are the server's cap on open live streams. The server counts a browser's streams per person (4) and per network address (16) on each instance and frees a slot when it notices the stream closed; on Vercel it never notices (five probe runs, no slot freed in 73 s), so slots are freed only when the stream's own timer ends it after four to five minutes. A tab that reloads a few times fills its own four; sixteen page loads from one office address fill the address's sixteen. The fix round made a refused tab keep saving over plain requests and reopen politely every 5 s, and that part works on the wire; but a page whose very first open is refused has no id to save with, and a stream that is refused or parked on the wrong instance still leaves the tab waiting for its acknowledgement. The burst saw it once in three runs (four writes stuck for a minute each), the decks row once in two.
2. The store budget you set holds, with one crack. Nothing refused: no "Too many requests", no timeout, no back off in the deployment's log through the whole pass; the smoke 40 of 40, the write probe green, the click model 18 of 18 twice, three full walks with every one of 900 writes answered inside 5 s. ## C3S.1 Verdict

The tree does not ship (FOCUS.md 6.2), and the gap has moved off the stream cap. On the deployment of record, deployed by the verifier from this tree, the core gate ran twice with no code change between: run 1 read 398 passed, 0 failed, 1 not driven (manual) of 399 in 35.6 min, and run 2, after the whole preview queue had warmed the deployment, read 395 passed, 3 failed, 1 manual in 36.7 min; under the round's rule (a row passes only when it passes in both runs) 395 rows pass, 3 are flaky and named (`export.pptx.perfect`, `images.insert.upload-while-pending`, `collab.presence-chips`: passed in run 1, failed in run 2), none failed in both, 1 is manual. Both walks drove all 316 steps on one deck with no stall, and a third walk under a 5 s window API bound drove them again with no call past 5 s (the "no Saving past 5 s" reading holds: 948 window API calls over three walks, every one answered inside its bound). Every row of the matrix passed on the memory tier as well: the local gate on 4395 (a private tmp store) and check step 32 on the check's own 4321 server both read 398 passed, 0 failed, 1 manual.

What the fix round closed, read first hand: the stream cap stall of C3-F1 in both of pass 1's faces. The bursts with three companions ran three times, 213 calls, none refused, none past 20 s, one past 5 s (9.8 s, settled by the gap watch's reopen); the runtime log holds no `stream refused` line through the two gates, the drives and the bursts (pass 1: 300, 240 of them `cap ip` from the companions) and no 500 (pass 1: nine, C3S-F4); `decks.access.paint` passed in both runs (pass 1: flaky). The stream probe read the mechanisms on the wire: a page shaped open (`TAB=1`) is admitted six of six times and four of four release cycles in three runs of three, the round's expectation; a refused open's body carries the minted client id on every 503; a raw held stream, the shape the product does not make, is still not freed within `retry-after` by the runtime but is closed by the reader liveness rule between 68 and 114 s after its open, where pass 1 read the lifetime timer at 240 to 290 s (SEAM-F4 narrowed to 1). `presence.spec.ts:215` and `realtime.spec.ts:543` pass on the check server (SEAM-F1 and SEAM-F8 closed), check step 5 is green under load (F-check5 closed), check step 21 gains five rows and step 31 seven.

What stops the ship now is three rows flaky on the warm deployment, two of them the server's: the editor's PPTX export polled on an instance that never held its job (C3S-F7, a product defect of the hosted export path), a second picture's acknowledgement settled by the gap watch at 8.4 s against the row's 5 s (C3S-F8, the last of C3S-F1's mechanism), and the presence chip row still closing its context under the leave beacon (C3S-F3, the driver's, SF-R1 not applied). Beside them: two spec rows written this round are red on their first run anywhere (`realtime.spec.ts:607`, C3S-F9; `presence.spec.ts:411`, C3S-F10), the standing chain reds (3 by design, 19, 21 with seven rows, 26 with three, 31 with nineteen budgets), the layout shift entries on `/edit` (C2-F12) and four unformatted files of the round (C3S-F11). On the memory tier `realtime.spec.ts` needed three runs on 4395 to reach its stream rows (`:234` and `:419` each failed once under a load of 11 to 13 from other work on the machine, C3S-F12); `presence.spec.ts:411` and `realtime.spec.ts:607` are red on both servers; `resize.spec.ts` 8 of 8, the A1 hand drive 18 of 18 twice, the two views clean on both origins, the new write probe green on the preview and one standing roster step short on the memory tier.

### C3S.2a The blob tier budget on the tree

The budget the fix round binds (one timed store call every 2 s per open deck per instance while a client stream is open, none otherwise; presence writes on a change alone at a 5 s floor with no retry loop; the SDK's retries off; a 429 or a 5xx backing the poll off to 60 s with the room telling its streams; nothing thrown by the store reaching the editor; every call under a deadline) was read again on this tree, by bytes and by constants. `git archive 540363f` (the checkpoint of the tree before the stream fix round) was unpacked into the scratchpad and every budget file compared with `cmp`: `packages/store/src/presence-store.ts`, `comments-store.ts`, `blob-store.ts`, `blob-vercel.ts`, `hosted.ts` and `packages/realtime/src/admission.ts` are byte identical to the checkpoint, and so is `packages/chrome/src/tokens.css` (and to `2b12e31`). Four budget files differ from the checkpoint by the fix round's lines and by nothing else, each read in the diff: `packages/realtime/src/blob.ts` (13 lines: `subscribe` tells a stream opened during an outage the standing `store` event at once, `queueMicrotask`, when `state.degraded`; a passive listener is told nothing; no new poll, no new call), `packages/store/src/pulse.ts` (6 lines: `isStoreBusy` reads the SDK's "Failed to fetch blob: <status>" as a refusal, so the ops and presence routes answer 503 `store_busy` with `retry-after` where C3S-F4 read a 500; no cadence), `packages/realtime/src/protocol.ts` (1 line: the hello's optional `covered`, a non negative seq) and `packages/realtime/src/channel.ts` (8 lines: the `covered` field's type and comment). No store call was added and no cadence changed on the stream path: the reader liveness reads the `presence` events the stream's subscription already receives and is judged at the heartbeat the route already runs; the tab token is a query parameter on an open the page already makes; the refusal body's `clientId` is a field on an answer the route already gives; the gap watch reopens a stream and resends nothing.

The constants read the values of pass 1's C3S.2a: `HOSTED_POLL_MS` 2000, `POLL_BACKOFF_MAX_MS` 60 000, `PULSE_SAFETY_TICKS` 15, `POLL_CALLS_PER_MINUTE_MAX` 30 (`pulse.ts` 23 to 29); `PRESENCE_POLL_MS` 5000, `PRESENCE_PUSH_SPACING_MS` 5000, `PRESENCE_SHARED_TTL_MS` 30 000, `PRESENCE_COPY_GRACE_MS` 60 000 (`presence-store.ts` 58 to 64); `BLOB_READ_TIMEOUT_MS` 10 000, `BLOB_DOCUMENT_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS` 20 000, `BLOB_WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS` 90 000, `TIMEOUT_GRACE_MS` 250, `CLAIM_GRACE_MS` 60 000, `CLAIM_RETRY_MS` 200 (`blob-store.ts` 450 to 598); `CAPS.streams` `{ anonymous: 4, signedIn: 8, agent: 4, ip: 16, instance: 256 }` untouched (`admission.ts` 39); `STREAM_LIFETIME_MS` 240 000 to 290 000 and `STREAM_HEARTBEAT_MS` 15 000 (`protocol.ts` 45, 47). ### C3S.3a The stream cap probe

What the probe measures (`verification/cycle3-ship-stream-cap-probe.mjs`, the verifier's; this pass adds two readings, both off by default so the raw reading stays comparable with pass 1 and the seam step): from one page of `/edit/gt-brand` (one anonymous identity with a stream of its own) six raw same origin stream fetches, held; every one closed client side and one open every 2, 5, 10, 20 and 30 s until admitted, and with `LONG_WAIT=1` at 45, 60 and 90 s more when the shorter ladder was refused (cumulative +112 to +202 s after the close), to read the reader liveness rule; then the release cycles (`RELEASE_CYCLES=4`): four times an open, held one second and closed, the next open waiting the last refusal's `retry-after` (5 s). With `TAB=1` every open carries `&tab=<32 hex>`, one token minted per run, the shape of the page's own opens since the fix round (a fresh token, so the page's own stream is never released by count). The caps are per instance (`admission.ts` `CAPS.streams`, `createStreamCounters` per process) and the preview routes each open to whichever instance is warm, so the runtime log's refusal line (`identity n/4, address n/16, instance n/256 (k identities)`) is the reading of the instance that refused. The page's own `describe().state.sync` read `connected: true, streamDown: false, storeDegraded: false, offline: false, pending 0, retained 0` before and after every run (the page's stream is not what the probe cuts). The round's expectation: a closed stream's slot frees within `retry-after`, so four opens of one identity after three closes succeed.

| Tab 1, 2, 3 (15:02Z to 15:04Z, `TAB=1`) | all six admitted in each run (the fourth, fifth and sixth included: each open released the token's earlier slots first)  | admitted at +2 s in each run                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | 4 of 4 admitted in each run                                                                                          | no `stream refused` line from 15:02:50Z through the three runs (the runtime log's next refusal is the warm raw run's at 16:14:06Z, 69 minutes later)                           | the round's expectation, for the shape the product uses: a fourth open of one identity after three closes succeeds, within `retry-after`, because the open carries the tab's token and `createStreamCounters.take` releases every slot the same tab and identity hold on the instance before the caps are judged (`room.ts` `releaseTab`, hello or not, whatever deck)                                      |
| Raw warm (16:13Z, after the 5 s walk)   | all six admitted (spread over the instances)                                                                             | refused at +2, +5, +10 and +20 s (four lines `identity 4/4, address 4/16, instance 4/256 (1 identities)` from 16:14:06Z to 16:14:42Z on the one instance that held four of them); admitted at +30 s (74 s into the run, 68 to 70 s after the opens; the log does not name where the admitted open landed) | 3 of 4 (cycle 1 refused at 16:15:17Z on the same counts; cycles 2 to 4 admitted)                                     | five `cap identity` lines, all `address 4/16 (1 identities)`; no `cap ip` line anywhere in the pass                                                                            | the same as raw 1 to 3: a raw stream's slot is held past `retry-after` and freed by the liveness rule about 70 to 115 s after its open, never by the lifetime timer in this pass                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

Read together: the runtime still reports neither the abort nor the cancel of a stream whose browser has gone (a raw held fetch closed client side is refused for at least 73 s, as in every run of pass 1 and the seam step), and the product no longer waits for the lifetime: a stream nobody posts presence for is closed at the heartbeat 75 to 90 s after its open (`createReaderLiveness`; read here between 68 and 114 s), a page's own opens release their tab's earlier slots at once (`?tab=`), a refused open carries a client id the page can post with, and a `leave` of the stream's own id closes it on the instance the beacon or a later open's `retire` lands on. The three shapes of pass 1's stall (a fresh context per load, C3S-F1; an open aborted before its hello, C3S-F2; a raw stream, SEAM-F4) are read against these releases in C3S.3's burst runs and C3S.5.

Severity as the orchestrator set it: 3 a core row broken (and, by the round's rule for this pass, a burst write past 20 s), 2 a core row flaky or a parked row visible by default (a red tree gate is filed at 2 as well), 1 cosmetic.
